name: CVBench
intro: CVBench是首个旨在严格评估跨视频关系推理能力的诊断基准。它包含1000个问答对，涵盖跨视频对象关联、跨视频事件关联和跨视频复杂推理三个层次。该基准挑战模型分析和整合来自动态视觉流的时空模式，并揭示了当前多模态大语言模型在跨视频理解方面的瓶颈。
org: Sun Yat-sen University, University of Hong Kong, Foshan University, University of Birmingham
build_method: 从 YouTube 检索 1,500 个候选视频，按跨视频关系、领域、时长和 720p/24fps 质量筛为 1,315 个，再经多级描述、GPT-4o 生成和两轮人工复核形成 1,000 题
metric: 准确率（总体、三个推理层级及 15 个子任务）
build_method_en: Retrieve 1,500 YouTube candidates; curate 1,315 by cross-video relations, domain, duration and 720p/24fps quality; then use hierarchical descriptions, GPT-4o synthesis and two-stage human review to produce 1,000 QA pairs
intro_en: CVBench is the first diagnostic benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate cross-video relational reasoning abilities. It contains 1,000 QA pairs covering three levels: cross-video object association, cross-video event association, and cross-video complex reasoning. The benchmark challenges models to analyze and integrate spatiotemporal patterns from dynamic visual streams, revealing current multimodal large language models' bottlenecks in cross-video understanding.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2508.19542 Sections 3.1–3.2, Figure 3, Tables 1–4 and the appendix validation description. CVBench defines three diagnostic tiers—cross-video object association, event association and complex reasoning—covering 15 subtasks. Task-driven YouTube retrieval yields 1,500 candidate videos. Eight annotators curate groups of two to four videos for multi-domain coverage, intrinsic relationships such as similarity, difference, causality and temporal order, primarily sub-10-minute duration, and at least 720p/24fps quality; gap filling and quality-driven replacement leave 1,315 videos. The four-stage QA pipeline adaptively samples frames and writes segment captions, aggregates video-level descriptions, builds relational summaries covering state transitions, causal links, complementarities and contradictions, and uses GPT-4o to generate at least two MCQs per group with one correct answer and three entity/temporal/causal distractors. Multi-model consensus validation checks hallucination and calibrates difficulty. First-stage review by eight annotators applies 15 task-specific criteria and can revise questions, fix options or recollect videos. Five new annotators independently re-examine 200 questions each for compliance, correctness and absence of hallucination; failed checks return for correction, yielding 1,000 QA pairs. Evaluation uses indexed multi-video inputs, eight frames per video for open models unless otherwise stated, zero-shot or chain-of-thought prompting, and Accuracy reported overall and by tier/subtask.
